summary: Nix research program phases 4+5 for one wave: sonnet deep dives per commissioned subtopic, pipelined into one opus consolidation (or revision) per group
logs: Wave 3: 4 dives across 4 groups (inputsx1, packagingx1, releasex1, generated-flakesx1); revising: inputs, packaging, release, generated-flakes
Wave 3 done: 4/4 groups consolidated · 43 MUST rules · 24 surprises · 19 follow-ups

top_rules: CI must run `nix flake check`/`show` with `-v` and enforce both a wall-clock timeout AND a 60s-max-gap between stage lines — never wall-clock alone, never without -v (nix-installer looked silent without -v, wasn't)

NIX-INP-02 upgrades SHOULD→MUST: on CppNix 2.35.2 (no lazy-trees), an unused root input still gets fetched and store-realized at lock time, unconditionally — confirmed via `nix path-info` on a never-touched input
Lix 2.95.2 supports `inputs.self.submodules` (behind flake-self-attrs) but has NO `self.lfs` at all ("attribute 'lfs' is not supported") — not the same gate, don't assume parity
`?submodules=1`/`?lfs=1` only work on git+https:/git+ssh: — the github: fetcher rejects both params outright with a scheme-mismatch error easy to misread as a rev typo
Before wrapping any third-party repo with submodules/lfs flags, grep its .gitattributes for unrelated filter=lfs content — grimoire's real repo broke Lix's clone via an unrelated LFS-tracked logo.png

nix-packaging.md's grimoire citation is wrong: the real remote is grimoire-rs/grimoire (public, verified via git ls-remote), not ocx-sh/grimoire (404) — and it has no flake.nix yet, so self.submodules can only be tested input-side today

#14339's floating-ref drift is now mechanically reproduced (not read from the issue): a dependency's own floating nixpkgs ref re-resolves to the branch's current drifted tip after follows removal; NIX-INP-08's --override-input restore is exact (rev+narHash match)
Same-tree path:.. from a test/ subdir to its parent is legal on both 2.31.5 and 2.35.2, and NIX-INP-04's exact grep (requiring a trailing slash) correctly does not false-positive on it
surprises: nix-installer's default-systems `nix flake check` is NOT silent when run with `-v`: it prints continuous hydraJobs matrix progress (max gap 34s over 300s) — the earlier 'silent hang' finding likely came from a run without -v, not from an actual hang

Grimoire's real repo (grimoire-rs/grimoire) has NO flake.nix at all as of 2026-09-27 — the self-submodules-remote open question's premise (a flake.nix declaring inputs.self.submodules) doesn't exist yet upstream

Grimoire's real repo independently uses Git LFS for assets/logo.png (unrelated to its two forked submodules), which broke Lix's plain git clone outright — a real-world LFS/submodule interaction no synthetic fixture had surfaced

The real HTTPS-LFS-remote test against microsoft/vscode-docs genuinely engaged Nix's LFS batch API (a real, non-mocked 429 from github.com) but was blocked by the sandbox's shared-egress GitHub rate limit, not by any protocol or Nix defect

The `github:` fetcher type outright rejects `submodules`/`lfs` URL parameters (parse error), forcing `git+https:` for any input needing either flag — this wasn't documented anywhere in the prior NIX-INP consolidation

Same-tree, never-referenced flake inputs are NOT lazily skipped on stock CppNix 2.35.2: `nix flake lock` alone fetches and store-realizes an input zero outputs ever touch, settling NIX-INP-02 as MUST rather than SHOULD

rule_ids: NIX-INP-01 — Decide nixpkgs follows by how each input is consumed; comment every deliberate non-follow
NIX-INP-02 — Keep library/module flake roots at zero inputs or nixpkgs-lib only; put test inputs in a sub-flake (SHOULD, MUST upgrade rejected)
NIX-INP-03 — Name a branch in url and let flake.lock carry the rev; freeze a rev only on purpose with a comment
NIX-INP-04 — Commit no local input; allow only relative path: that stays inside the flake's own git tree, floor 2.26 (MUST)
NIX-INP-05 — Give every input an explicit scheme; no indirect names, no nixexprs.tar.xz; FlakeHub deferred to NIX-REL-06 (MUST)
NIX-INP-06 — Track a flake-checker-supported nixpkgs branch under 30 days old, advisory CEL check
NIX-INP-07 — Move entries with nix flake update <input>; never --update-input or --recreate-lock-file (MUST)
NIX-INP-08 — Re-lock and read the diff after any follows edit; restore a drifted dependency nixpkgs rev with --override-input
NIX-INP-09 — Declare inputs.self.submodules/lfs when the build reads them; Lix leg adds flake-self-attrs and marks self.lfs expected-fail (MUST)
NIX-INP-10 — Keep builtin fetchers unreachable from outputs; use inputs or FOD fetchers
NIX-INP-11 — Refresh the lock weekly via a scheduled, SHA-pinned workflow that opens a PR
NIX-INP-12 — Consider an --override-input nixpkgs-unstable CI leg for widely consumed flakes; never commit it
NIX-INP-13 — Run CI eval with -v and timestamps; treat a >60 s line gap as an alarm naming the stalled step, never a kill (new, SHOULD advisory)
NIX-INP-14 — Wrap a non-flake repo needing submodules/LFS as a git+https: flake=false input with rev and submodules=1/lfs=1, never github: (new, SHOULD)

top_rules: ocx builds end to end under buildRustPackage (cargoBuildFlags = ["-p" "ocx" "-p" "ocx_shim"], pkg-config only) — both binaries installed and stripped, watched green.

Correction to nix-packaging.md's V-fb #11: ocx's Cargo.lock has 10 git-sourced packages (astral-sh/uv x9, pubgrub x1), not 0 — needs exactly 2 outputHashes entries, keyed by commit SHA not per-package.
ocx has no -V/--version flag (no #[command(version)] on its clap Cli); versionCheckHook needs versionCheckProgramArg = "version" (the subcommand), watched red on "--version" and green on "version".

GATE-10's real per-PR cost is rustc compilation (~6-7 min), not crate vendoring; a metadata-only package.nix edit still forces a full rebuild because buildRustPackage is one non-incremental derivation.

aws-lc-sys's cmake wrapper crate compiles unconditionally regardless of whether a real cmake binary runs; get_builder() picks CcBuilder (no cmake invoked) whenever bindgen isn't required and no FIPS/sanitizer/override applies, so NIX-PKG-17's pkg-config-only recipe is target-conditional, not target-independent.

M-D-27 answered and watched red/green: ship both a pythonPackagesExtensions overlay (reaches every interpreter's pythonN.pkgs) and a top-level packages.<system>.<name> bound to python3; top-level-only fails eval (attribute missing) for any other interpreter.

M-D-24 (build.rs determinism) reads deterministic-by-construction (CI unset, no .git in the fileset src) but was never empirically confirmed via nix build --rebuild before an environment fault ended the dive — stays open, not promoted to MUST.

NIX-PKG-16 as a checks derivation was drafted (ok/bad fixtures, builtins.compareVersions) but never built — flagged NOT RUN rather than fabricated, along with closure size and the --rebuild determinism check.
surprises: nix-packaging.md's own prior verification claim ("0 git dependencies in ocx's Cargo.lock") was wrong: re-running the identical grep on the live repo returns 10, from astral-sh/uv and astral-sh/pubgrub git deps pulled in via ocx_python.

ocx's CLI has no --version flag at all — it only reports its version through a custom `version` subcommand, which silently broke the standard versionCheckHook default ("unexpected argument '--version' found", not an obviously-packaging-related error).

A single non-source attribute change (just versionCheckProgramArg) forced a full ~6-7 minute recompile of all ~300 crates, because buildRustPackage is one non-incremental derivation — warming the cargo-vendor-dir derivation saved the fetch step but not the dominant compile cost.

The Rust `cmake` wrapper crate compiles in every aws-lc-sys build regardless of whether a real `cmake` binary is ever invoked; the actual cc-vs-cmake choice is gated by is_bindgen_required()/FIPS/sanitizer/override deep in aws-lc-sys's own builder/main.rs, not by cmake's mere presence in Cargo.lock.

The shared research-lang Nix toolchain (run.sh, .nix-portable, conf, all fixtures) was progressively deleted mid-dive by an apparently concurrent sibling wave-3 process, cutting three verifications short (closure size, --rebuild determinism, the PKG-16 checks-derivation build) as a genuine, externally-caused environment fault rather than anything this session did.

GitHub's REST API returned schema-shaped type stubs instead of real JSON values for directory-listing calls in this sandbox's curl (api.github.com), while raw.githubusercontent.com file fetches and codeload.github.com tarballs worked normally — a sandbox quirk worth knowing before assuming a GitHub API 'empty' result means the path doesn't exist.

rule_ids: NIX-PKG-01 — Fetch src with a nixpkgs fetcher and SRI hash = "sha256-…"; never builtins, sha256 =, cargoSha256 or vendorSha256 (SHOULD)
NIX-PKG-02 — Pin git sources with a full 40-hex rev or a real tag; never short hex, a branch, or tag = "<hex>" (MUST)
NIX-PKG-03 — Never hand-write a hash; use nurl/nix-prefetch or lib.fakeHash and copy the got: value (MUST)
NIX-PKG-04 — On any fetcher-argument change, reset hash and verify with nix build --rebuild .#<pkg>.src (MUST)
NIX-PKG-05 — Filter src with lib.fileset.toSource over an explicit list; never src = ./. or self unfiltered (MUST)
NIX-PKG-06 — Keep package.nix at the root as a plain by-name-ready callPackage function with no ../ references (SHOULD)
NIX-PKG-07 — Set meta.description (nixpkgs grammar), license, platforms and homepage on every package (MUST presence, SHOULD grammar)
NIX-PKG-08 — Give meta.license as lib.licenses.<attr> or a single SPDX id, never a compound expression; eval with abort-on-warn (MUST; rationale corrected: the fleet is Apache-2.0)
NIX-PKG-09 — Put build tools in nativeBuildInputs and libraries in buildInputs, with strictDeps = true (MUST)
NIX-PKG-10 — Set __structuredAttrs = true, keep env.* scalar, and put lists at the top level (SHOULD)
NIX-PKG-11 — Wrap every overridden phase in runHook pre/post and never set phases (MUST)
NIX-PKG-12 — Use --replace-fail/--replace-warn, never bare --replace (MUST)
NIX-PKG-13 — Give every A CLI versionCheckHook with doInstallCheck, pointed at its real version entry point; put behaviour tests in passthru.tests (MUST; scope revised)
NIX-PKG-14 — Use mkDerivation (finalAttrs: …) only when self-referencing, otherwise a plain attrset; never rec for finalPackage (SHOULD)
NIX-PKG-15 — Build in-repo Rust with buildRustPackage and cargoLock.lockFile = ./Cargo.lock; never read the lock through ${src} or builtins.path self (MUST)
NIX-PKG-16 — Build with pinned nixpkgs rustPlatform plus a rustc-floor check against rust-toolchain.toml as a CI step, with no rust-overlay in package.nix (SHOULD; the checks form is unwatched)
NIX-PKG-17 — Start native inputs at pkg-config and add tools only when an error names them; the aws-lc-sys recipe holds only on the cc-builder path (SHOULD; scope revised)
NIX-PKG-18 — Package Python with buildPythonPackage { pyproject = true; build-system = [ <backend> ]; } and use uv2nix only for compiled runtime deps (SHOULD)
NIX-PKG-19 — Confirm versionCheckHook's entry point, set versionCheckProgramArg when the CLI lacks --version, and never disable the check (MUST, new)
NIX-PKG-20 — Budget GATE-10's Rust build as a full recompile for any package edit, and do not count vendor caching as a saving (CONSIDER, new)
NIX-PKG-21 — Export a Python library through a pythonPackagesExtensions overlay plus a top-level package, never top-level only (MUST, new)
NIX-PKG-22 — Set cargoLock.outputHashes with one fake-hash-derived entry per git revision when Cargo.lock has git sources, and no allowBuiltinFetchGit (SHOULD, new)

top_rules: MUST (escalated from SHOULD): rev/tag in a version-tracking package.nix must be interpolated (rev = "v${finalAttrs.version}") — a literal ref lets nix-update bump version and rewrite hash to match stale, unrelated content, undetectable by diff
Never trust 'the hash also changed' as proof a nix-update version bump was correct — the hash always matches whatever was actually fetched, correct or stale

Grep for leftover lib.fakeHash/lib.fakeSha256 after any nix-update -F run — nix-update text-matches the OLD evaluated hash VALUE, not the symbol, so a symbolic placeholder silently never gets replaced (exit 0, no warning)
When priming a hash for nix-update to auto-discover, write the literal SRI placeholder text, not the lib.fakeHash symbol, if write-back must happen automatically

The nested-bwrap 'cannot rename: Permission denied' during hash discovery is real but harmless — Nix prints it as error (ignored) and still emits the got: hash line nix-update needs; it is not what blocked the write-back

Prefer nixpkgs's tag= over rev= for a real tag (nixpkgs's own fetchers docs state this preference); nix-update treats tag and rev identically given interpolation, so REL-13's example moves to tag with no write-back cost
REL-09's README block (nix profile add + install fallback) needs no per-implementation variant: confirmed identical exit-code behavior on CppNix 2.31.5, 2.35.2, and Lix 2.95.2

REL-16's smoke test generalizes cleanly from git+file: to a real pushed github: tag (Mic92/nixpkgs-review/4.0.0) — run it against the real ref whenever the tag is already pushed, not just a local twin
surprises: The wave-1 'cannot rename: Permission denied' report was a red herring: it's a real, reproducible nested-bwrap-sandbox artifact (same class as NixOS/nix#4295) that Nix itself labels 'error (ignored)', and it never blocked hash discovery — the true cause of the missing write-back is nix-update's replace_hash doing a verbatim text match against the OLD evaluated hash VALUE, which never equals the literal source text 'lib.fakeHash'

REL-13's existing verification method ('confirm rev or the hash changed too') is provably insufficient: a literal, non-interpolated rev/tag causes nix-update to bump version AND rewrite hash to match the stale, un-bumped content — both attributes change, git diff looks like a normal correct update, and nix build succeeds, silently shipping the wrong source under a new version number
This silent-corruption failure mode argues REL-13 should be escalated from SHOULD to MUST, since the defect is undetectable by the diff-based check the consolidation currently relies on

tag= and rev= are fully interchangeable from nix-update's perspective (both the correct-write-back and the silent-stale-content failure reproduce identically on both), settling map conflict E24 cleanly

Determinate Nix 3.22.5 cannot be measured from this corpus at all: the pinned nixpkgs 26.11pre packages only 'fh' (the FlakeHub CLi), no determinate-nix attribute exists anywhere in nixVersions or top-level — it is installer-distributed, not a nixpkgs derivation

The flake-compat bridge and README profile-add/install lines showed zero new implementation divergence beyond what C3 already found — Lix 2.95.2 and CppNix 2.31.5 are otherwise drop-in equivalent for every command tested

rule_ids: NIX-REL-01 — Read version from the project's own manifest through a source-tree path (./Cargo.toml, ./pyproject.toml); never a literal, never via ${src}
NIX-REL-02 — Emit the manifest version verbatim; never append a pre<date>_<rev>, +rev, -dirty or -unstable suffix, not even conditionally
NIX-REL-03 — Do not read self.rev/shortRev/dirtyShortRev/lastModified/revCount in an exported derivation; accept drvPath churn only as a knowing opt-in
NIX-REL-04 — Where self metadata is read, use self.shortRev or self.dirtyShortRev or "unknown"; never expect rev under path: or revCount under github:
NIX-REL-05 — Ship default.nix/shell.nix through github:NixOS/flake-compat (flake = false) only; never edolstra or nix-community flake-compat
NIX-REL-06 — Take no FlakeHub input and run no flakehub-push in fleet flakes; FlakeHub publishers publish tagged releases only
NIX-REL-07 — Release by the project's existing vX.Y.Z tags; invent no flake-only version; document github:<owner>/<repo>/vX.Y.Z; D flakes version by lock revision
NIX-REL-08 — Refresh flake.lock in its own commit before the tag; the tag commit never modifies flake.lock
NIX-REL-09 — Give A/D READMEs nix run, nix profile add with an install fallback comment, and an input snippet; never nix-env -i or --accept-flake-config
NIX-REL-10 — Rename or remove outputs over two releases behind the warning mechanism that fits (lib.warn, warnOnInstantiate, tree map, mkRenamedOptionModule)
NIX-REL-11 — Never pass abort-on-warn to nix flake check or a whole-flake build; scope it to named current attributes
NIX-REL-12 — State compatibility as pinned CppNix + NIX-GATE-16 floor + Lix advisory + Determinate untested + flakes experimental (RFC 136)
NIX-REL-13 — Interpolate a forge fetcher's ref from finalAttrs.version (tag = "v${finalAttrs.version}"); never a literal version-shaped rev/tag; verify the fetched URL contains the version
NIX-REL-14 — Keep fleet CLIs nixpkgs-ready without submitting: by-name package.nix (NIX-PKG-06), three-attribute swap, updateScript or opt-out comment
NIX-REL-15 — Stand up no public substituter; if one exists, document the nix.conf pair as explicit opt-in and never call nixConfig automatic
NIX-REL-16 — Before announcing, nix run the pushed github:<owner>/<repo>/<tag> from a clean store and require --version to print the version
NIX-REL-17 — Leave a literal SRI hash for nix-update, never the lib.fakeHash symbol, and grep for leftover fake-hash symbols after every run

top_rules: autoPatchelfHook goes on every *-linux package unconditionally (gate on stdenv.hostPlatform.system, never on a libc tag) — libc tagging drifts and the hook is a no-op on static ELFs
A bare-only first-match platform selector silently drops amazon/corretto (glibc+musl, no bare offer) and misroutes astral-sh/ruff to the wrong manifest — measured on real index data, not hypothetical

Never write '$${var}' expecting one literal $ plus interpolation: Nix's indented and double-quoted strings both treat bare $$ before { as an escape for literal ${, silently killing the interpolation — build the splice by string concatenation instead

A translator implements only the interpolation-token forms a live census confirms are used (121/122 real values use bare ${installPath}; every other documented form is 0/122) — untested forms stay a throw, not speculative plumbing
An entrypoint launcher must wrap the package's own already-env-composed binary, never the raw pre-wrapper payload, or every declared env var silently vanishes for that one entry point

A generated package's meta.description/meta.homepage come from the ocx package index's own desc.description/upstream.repository_url fields, never from OCI annotations — 0/1720 image indexes carry description or url at all

org.opencontainers.image.source is not a homepage: it names the ocx-contrib mirror repository, present on 98.3% of packages, and mapping it to meta.homepage would misdirect every consumer to the wrong repo

nix run on a multi-binary package with no mainProgram does not 'resolve' — it fails loudly looking for $out/bin/<pname> — so no rule or doc example may claim nix run <flake>#<multi-bin-pkg> works without having actually run it
surprises: NIX-GEN-16's own specified verification grep (checking for 'contents: write'/'git push'/'create-pull-request') is not admissible: it matches both a direct-push twin and a PR-based twin, since a PR action legitimately needs contents: write too — the rule needs a two-stage check (git-push files that never also mention a PR-creation action)

Fixing NIX-GEN-20's shell-injection bug introduced a second, unrelated Nix escaping bug: writing the corrected splice as one indented-string literal ($${var}) silently disabled interpolation entirely, because Nix treats bare $$ before { as an escape for literal ${ — this is undocumented-feeling behavior that produces no error, just wrong output

ghcr.io's manifest endpoint (not the blob endpoint) 404s without an explicit Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json header even with a valid bearer token — indistinguishable from a genuinely missing digest unless you know to add it

amazon/corretto has glibc and musl linux/amd64 offers but literally no bare manifest at all, so any generator that assumes every package has a bare fallback silently drops a real, currently-shipping package

0/1720 OCI image indexes in the ocx index carry org.opencontainers.image.description or .url — the D-shape description/homepage requirement can only ever be satisfied from the ocx package index's own metadata file, never from the OCI layer NIX-GEN-14 already reads for license

kitware/cmake's real per-platform config blobs genuinely differ (PATH=${installPath}/bin on linux vs ${installPath}/CMake.app/Contents/bin on darwin), confirming the 'two registry hops per platform, never copy one platform's blob onto another' rule with live data rather than an assumption

release/verification-rerun-w3: REL-13's existing verification method ('confirm rev or the hash changed too') is provably insufficient: a literal, non-interpolated rev/tag causes nix-update to bump version AND rewrite hash to match the stale, un-bumped content — both attributes change, git diff looks like a normal correct update, and nix build succeeds, silently shipping the wrong source under a new version number

release/verification-rerun-w3: This silent-corruption failure mode argues REL-13 should be escalated from SHOULD to MUST, since the defect is undetectable by the diff-based check the consolidation currently relies on
